subject: Pen test report acceptance window, methodology, and evidence requirements
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: laura.hensley@acme.com, acme-security@acmecorp.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-14T09:08:00-08:00
Subject: Pen test report acceptance window, methodology, and evidence requirements

Laura / Acme team —

Thanks for taking a look at our SIG / SOC 2 package. A couple of quick items we want to confirm so we can close the evidence loop on your questionnaire:

1) Report age: We have a vendor report authored by BlueHarbor Security dated 2026-11-15 (summary attached). Does Acme require the pen test to be within 12 months of the SOC 2 audit date, or do you accept reports up to 15 months old when a documented remediation + retest plan is in place?

2) Methodology/firm credentials: Acme’s questionnaire asks for firm credentials and sampling methodology. The BlueHarbor engagement was a mixed manual/automated assessment focused on externally-facing services and customer data planes; internal admin networks were excluded due to segmentation controls (we can provide the scoping statement). What level of detail do you need in the vendor workpapers vs. a summary-only report?

3) Evidence types for remediation: For fixes we plan to provide: ticket references, config diffs, and retest verification from the vendor. Will that be acceptable, or do you require full raw workpapers? Also any preference on retest window (we were planning 45–90 days after remediation for high/critical items).

I’ve cc’d Karthik and Mina to confirm vendor creds and the proposed retest cadence.

Next steps: if useful, I can schedule a short call this week to walk through the BlueHarbor scope and the remediation tracker.

Attachments: BlueHarbor_Summary_2026-11.pdf

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

From: Laura Hensley <laura.hensley@acme.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: acme-security@acmecorp.com, vendor-ops@acmecorp.com
Date: 2027-02-14T12:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report acceptance window, methodology, and evidence requirements

Jordan —

Thanks for the overview. Short answers first:

- Report age: our standard policy is 12 months, but we have flexibility to accept a report up to 15 months old when we can see an active remediation plan and a scheduled retest for high/critical items. That needs to be documented in the vendor plan and tracked in your ticketing system.

- Methodology & firm creds: we require a vendor statement of methodology (manual vs automated split, sampling approach) and evidence that the firm meets industry accreditations (e.g., CREST, OSCP roster, or equivalent). CVs for the lead tester and company profile are helpful. A summary report is acceptable if accompanied by vendor workpapers under NDA.

- Evidence types: priority is (1) vendor retest verification showing the same test case failed then passed, (2) remediation tickets with owner and dates, and (3) config diffs or screenshots for config changes. We appreciate when customers supply a remediation tracker with links to artifacts.

I’m attaching a short PDF that lists our evidence requirements and preferred formats. If you can provide the remediation tracker and proposed retest date by next week, we can provisionally accept the 2026-11 report.

Attachments: Acme_Evidence_Req_20270214.pdf

Best,
Laura Hensley
Senior InfoSec Manager — Third-Party Risk
Acme Corp
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-15T08:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report acceptance window, methodology, and evidence requirements

Jordan / team —

Quick vendor/tech note to support the thread: BlueHarbor Security performed the engagement (engagements@blueharborsec.com). Highlights for Acme:

- Credentials: BlueHarbor is CREST-aligned, lead tester has OSCP + CREST certs; company holds cyber insurance and maintains a conflict-of-interest attestation. I’ll attach their summary PDF in the shared drive.

- Methodology: mixed manual + automated; manual review targeted owner-identified high-risk endpoints and customer-facing APIs; automated scans covered the canonical infrastructure surface. The scoping statement explicitly excluded segmented admin VLANs and internal CI/CD runners — we documented compensating controls (network ACLs, dedicated bastion, and VPC peering restrictions).

- Retest recommendation: for critical findings we usually aim for a vendor re-test 30–60 days after remediation verification; for medium/low items 60–90 days. If Acme prefers a single retest window, suggest 60 days for critical/medium combined.

Action items I can own: upload BlueHarbor CVs and the scoping statement to the Drive, and create a remediation tracker template (ticket links + evidence field). Jordan — tell me if you want the tracker in spreadsheet or a simple Google Sheet.

—
Karthik Iyer
Security PM, Redwood Inference
From: vendor-ops@acmecorp.com <vendor-ops@acmecorp.com>

Cc: laura.hensley@acme.com
Date: 2027-02-22T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report acceptance window, methodology, and evidence requirements

Jordan / Karthik —

Two clarifications from Acme vendor ops:

1) NDA for workpapers: Acme will accept summary-only reports if the vendor is willing to sign a limited-scope NDA to release workpapers to Acme third-party security reviewers. If BlueHarbor can sign, please share contact and draft NDA.

2) Evidence granularity: for high and critical items we require either (a) vendor re-test evidence (test case, timestamp, tester), or (b) remediation workpapers showing root cause analysis + config diffs. Screenshots alone are low confidence unless accompanied by logs or commit ids.

If you can provide the vendor contact and proposed retest date(s) by 3/3 I’ll mark the report as provisionally acceptable in our intake system.

Regards,
Acme Vendor Ops
